validation_reason: Oracle reproduced the vulnerability and detected the maintainer fix.

vulnerable.evidence: Forged x-middleware-subrequest header survived filterInternalHeaders without a valid subrequest id, allowing middleware authorization bypass

fixed.evidence: Forged x-middleware-subrequest header was stripped because the subrequest id did not match the server secret, blocking the bypass

oracle.explanation: The oracle loads next's internal filterInternalHeaders utility (packages/next/src/server/lib/server-ipc/utils.ts), the exact function patched for CVE-2025-29927/GHSA-f82v-jwr5-mffw. It first proves the function works correctly on a benign header set with no internal middleware headers, confirming normal operation and setting operation_completed=true only after that succeeds. It then calls the same function with a forged 'x-middleware-subrequest' header (the attacker-controlled header used to make the server believe a request is an internal middleware-originated subrequest, thereby skipping middleware execution and any authorization logic it implements) accompanied by a bogus 'x-middleware-subrequest-id' that cannot match the real per-process secret. In the vulnerable version (15.2.2), filterInternalHeaders has no concept of a subrequest id and never strips 'x-middleware-subrequest', so the forged header survives, demonstrating the bypass primitive (exploit_succeeded=true). In the patched version (>=15.2.3/13.5.9), the function validates 'x-middleware-subrequest-id' against a secret and deletes 'x-middleware-subrequest' when it doesn't match, neutralizing the forged header (exploit_succeeded=false). The test only requires the installed next package and node:path, performs no process spawning, network I/O, or filesystem writes outside the module's own resolution, and prints a single ORACLE_RESULT JSON line reflecting the outcome.
